author: Cunningham
asr_identification: Great Temple and Bodhi tree at Buddha-Gaya (Bodh Gaya, Gaya district)
evidence: Bodhi tree still standing on a raised terrace; temple c. 50 ft square, 160-170 ft high, with tiers of niches holding plaster Buddhas; pedestal of the lost statue measured 13 ft 2 in x 5 ft 8 in x 4 ft vs Xuanzang's 12 ft 5 in by 4 ft 2 in; eastern doorway; Amara Deva inscription matches the Brahman founder story; Faxian's stone identified with a blue circular stone in the Vageswari Devi temple
quote: Several of the obiects enumerated by the Chinese pilgrim I have been able to identify from their exact correspondence with his description…Its dimensions are as follows : length 13 feet 2 inches,' breadth 5 feet 8 inches, and height 4 feet…I feel satisfied that the present lofty temple is the identical one that was built by tbe celebrated Amara Sinba about A. D. 600.
note: Agrees with Mizutani and with AG 1871 (Great Temple = Xuanzang's vihara). Dates the temple to Amara Simha c. A.D. 500-600 (later abandoned view).

author: Cunningham
note: History of the Buddha-Gaya temple from the Burmese inscription (Brahman of Xuanzang = Pentha-gu-gyi); not a location argument.

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: Buchhokar Tal, small tank SE of the Great Temple, Buddha-Gaya
evidence: tank SE of the temple; also notes the granite railing pillars found c. 60 yards E of the temple, perhaps from the milk-rice stupa (SW of the temple per Xuanzang)
quote: To the south-east of the Great Temple there is a small tank called Biiclholcar Tdl, which exactly answers the description given by the Chinese pilgrim of the tank of the dragon Muchalmda.i This agreement is so striking, that it was seen at once by the members of the Burmese Embassy.
note: Differs from Mizutani (Urel tank, S of the temple). AG 1871 gives no identification for this site in places.tsv.

author: Cunningham
name_in_asr: Elephant of Perfume (gandha-hasti) stupa and pillar; sacred tank
asr_identification: Bakror, across the Phalgu/Lilajan from Buddha-Gaya (Gaya district)
evidence: ruined stupa and stump of the pillar at Bakror; shaft said to be removed to Gaya, where a sandstone pillar 2 ft diam. and 16 ft high stands in Sahebganj (set up 1789); tank = Marttand Pokhar / Suraj Kund (Buddhakund)
quote: The tope and pillar of Bakror were visited by Hwen Thsang, who relates a story regarding the capture by a certain king of an " Elephant of Perfume” ( gandha-liasti)…There was also a sacred tank, which is, perhaps, represented by a small walled tank generally called Mdrttand JPohhar
note: Agrees with Mizutani (Bakror) and AG 1871. The pillar of 09.01.02 (Udraka) is not separated from the elephant pillar here.

author: Cunningham
note: Footnote reference to Julien under the Bakror/Punawa pages; Punawa itself not identified with a Xiyu ji place.

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: three bare hills 1/2 mile N of Kurkihar (Gaya district); Giryek hill on the Panchana
evidence: three rugged hills touching at their bases half a mile N of the village; Giryek: brick stupa Jarasandha-ka-baithak 28 ft diam., 21 ft high on a 14-ft base, shaft sunk 41 ft and gallery driven, nothing found; tank 100 ft square near it
quote: There are, however, three bare and rugged hills which rise boldly out of the plain about half a mile to tke north of the village. As these three hills touch one another at their bases, I think that they may fairly he identified with the three-peaked hill of Hwen Tlisang.
note: Kukkutapada: agrees with Mizutani (hill 1 mile N of Kurkihar) and AG 1871. Kurkihar itself matched with Fa-Hian's account.

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: Giryek hill (Indrasilaguha), Jarasandha's Tower = goose (hamsa) stupa; Vipula-giri at Rajgir
evidence: only one stupa on the hill, as in Xuanzang; broken figure with a goose on its pedestal found close by; lac seals with stupa bearing a goose; bearing and distance agree; Giryek < Giri-eka; ruined stupa/chaitya on Vipula summit
quote: If niy identification of the Giryek Hill with the Indrasila-guha of Hwen Thsang is correct, there can be little doubt that J arasandha’s Tower is the very stupa that was built in honour of the devoted goose…close by T found a ^(.broken figure with a large goose carved on the pedestal
note: Agrees with Mizutani and AG 1871 (Giryek). Goose stupa has no separate id. The Gidhadwar cavern in the S face (p. 18; no hit in this batch) is AG's Indrasilaguha cave.

author: Cunningham
name_in_asr: old city between the hills (Kusagarapura); new Rajagriha; Vipula
asr_identification: Old Rajgir (valley girdled by five hills) and New Rajgir fort, Bihar (Patna district)
evidence: survey of the old ramparts: circuit 24,500 ft (4 2/3 mi) vs Faxian 24-28 li and Xuanzang 30 li; outer wall over the hills traced, 13 ft thick; inter-hill distances totalling 41,000 ft, so Xuanzang's 150 li emended to 50 li; new town an irregular pentagon, 14,260 ft circuit outside the ditches, with citadel 2,000 x 1,500 ft
quote: My survey of the ancient ramparts gives a circuit of 24,500 feet, or 4|th miles, which is between the two statements of the Chinese pilgrims…Por this 1 imher T propose to read 50 li or 8^ miles, a correction which is n isolutely necessary to make the statement tallv with the inoasm-omente of my survey.
note: Agrees with Mizutani and AG 1871; the emendation 150 > 50 li for the outer wall is argued here.

author: Cunningham
name_in_asr: stupa 60 ft with stone pillar 50 ft
asr_identification: circular hollow mound outside the SW corner of New Rajgir; Son Bhandar cave in Baibhar
evidence: large circular hollow mound (bricks removed) like the excavated stupa at Sarnath; Son Bhandar cave 34 x 17 ft with inscriptions
quote: According to Hwen Thsang’s accomit, this circular hollow was the site of a stupa 60 fe?t in hei-ht there .vyas a stone nSlar oO feet high
note: Mizutani places 09.02.17a near the present Baitarni Godan; not in AG 1871 (places.tsv).

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: Baragaon ruins (Nalanda); Kulika = ruined mound near Jagdispur 1 1/4 mile SW of Baragaon
evidence: two inscriptions naming Nalanda found on the site; Jagdispur mound 200 ft square with a 70-ft-square eminence; large sculpture (15 x 9.5 ft) of the Buddha under the Bodhi tree; Kalapinaka placed c. 4 miles SE of Nalanda (no site named)
quote: This place I was able to identify witli a ruined mound near Jagdisinir, at mile to the south-west of the ruins of Baragaon.
note: Kolika (09.03.08): Mizutani gives no modern identification; AG 1871 repeats Jagdispur. Nalanda agrees with Mizutani.

author: Cunningham
name_in_asr: Nalanda monastery; temple W of the monastery; stupas; Avalokitesvara statue
asr_identification: Baragaon: monastery ruins 1,600 x 400 ft; mound A (Punwa mound) = temple where Buddha preached 3 months; mounds B, C = stupa and Avalokitesvara statue
evidence: monastery traced by square cultivated patches (court-yards of six monasteries); mound A 63 ft high, excavated to 17 ft exposing temple walls; inscribed stones of 6th-7th c.; tank Karnidya = Naga pool
quote: show tbe positions of the court-yards of the six smaller monasteries whiob are described by Hwen Thsang as being situated within one enclosure forming altogether eight courts…This temple I would identify with the ruined mound marked A, still 63 feet in height
note: Sub-sites of Nalanda not separately in the master table. Agrees with Mizutani on Nalanda.; 09.03.06 added (mound A = the three-month temple)

author: Cunningham
name_in_asr: Great Vihar; Avalokitesvara temple; Baladitya's vihar; Tara Bodhisattva vihar; well
asr_identification: Baragaon: mound G (Avalokitesvara temple), mound H E of the Dehar tank (Baladitya's vihar), mound with 70.5 x 67 ft base (Tara vihar), well P
evidence: mound H 45 ft high, 60 ft broad at top; colossal ascetic Buddha at Baithak Bhairav at its foot; excavated base of Tara vihar 70.5 x 67 ft on terrace 6 ft high, 125 ft square; large well P S of it; inscribed images (Sariputra, Maudgalyayana)
quote: A mound, marked H., to the east of the Debar Tank, corresponds exactly with the situation of this temple. It is still 45 feet in height
note: Sub-sites of Nalanda (no separate ids).

author: Cunningham
note: Ghosrawa: Avalokitesvara statue compared iconographically with the one at the Kapotika monastery; no location argued.

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: Titarawa (not a Xiyu ji place)
evidence: mound 20 ft high with walls of a large monastery; colossal Buddha with inscription naming Mahapala
quote: There is no mention of this place either in Ea-Hian or Hwen Thsang.
note: Revised in AG 1871, which identifies 09.03.15 (place of the Buddha's preaching) with the great mound of Titarawa; Mizutani: no settled identification.

author: Cunningham
note: Barabar: size of a colossal Buddha compared with Xuanzang's statue at Buddha-Gaya; no location.

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: Barabar caves (Gaya district); not identified with any place of Xuanzang
evidence: Ananta Varmma inscription calls a cave Pravara-giri-guha; caves occupied by Brahmans by the 6th-7th c., explaining Xuanzang's silence
quote: occupation hy Brahmans in the seventh century may account for the silence of the Chinese pilgrim Hwen Thsang regarding the caves
note: Mizutani identifies 08.04.02 (Pravaragiri) with Barabar Hill; Cunningham records the name Pravara-giri but does not connect it with Xuanzang; AG 1871 puts the mountain between Giryek and Gaya.

author: Cunningham
name_in_asr: famous spring of holy water 30 li N of Gaya
asr_identification: Patal Ganga spring at the foot of Barabar hill (Gaya district)
evidence: no spring N of Gaya nearer than Barabar; road distance 21 miles; annual bathing fair of 20,000-50,000 in Bhadrapada (Buchanan)
quote: I would suggest that Hwen Thsang’s distance of 3< > li should be corrected to 130 li (or 21f miles), wRich would make his famous spring agree exactly with the position of the Fatal Ganga
note: The spring is part of the Gaya section (no separate id). Emendation 30 > 130 li.

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: Besarh (Muzaffarpur district), with the fort Raja Bisal ka garh; city including Bakhra
evidence: 27 miles N of Patna, 20 from Hajipur; fort 1,580 x 750 ft inside, 4,660 ft round the crest (palace 4-5 li in Xuanzang); name Besarh in the Ain-i Akbari; old city circuit 12 miles enclosing Besarh and Bakhra
quote: This almost perfect coincidence of name, position, and dimensions, see'ms quite sufficient to place the idjentifi-; cation of Besarh with Yaiiali beyond all reasonable doubt.
note: Agrees with Mizutani (Basarh) and AG 1871.

author: Cunningham
name_in_asr: stupas S of the town (Amradarika's garden etc.)
asr_identification: brick mound with the tomb of Mir Abdal, SW of the Besarh fort
evidence: solid brick mound 23 ft 8 in high, c. 1,000 ft from the SW angle of the fort
quote: This brick mound is the ruin of one of the stupas, or solid towers of Vaisali, of which so many are described by Hwen Thsang.
note: Identification only as one of the six stupas S of the city; Mizutani gives no identification for 07.03.07.

author: Cunningham
name_in_asr: Asoka stupa and lion pillar; Monkey Tank (Markata-hrada)
asr_identification: Bakhra lion pillar and surrounding remains, NW of Besarh
evidence: ruined stupa N of the pillar, small tank S of it, two low mounds W and S of the tank (honey stupas), mound NW (monkey statue); bevelled bricks; inscribed statue 8th-9th c.
quote: The lion pillar anchthe surrounding remains at Bakhra I would identify witli a ^‘oup of holy buildings described by Hwen Thsang as being situated upwards of one mile to the iiorth-westfbf the Palace of Vaislli
note: Agrees with Mizutani and AG 1871.

author: Cunningham
name_in_asr: lion pillar; place of the second synod; Kutagara hall
asr_identification: Bakhra (pillar; Mahavana); no remains found for the synod site SE of the city
evidence: lion 4 ft 6 in, capital 3 ft 10 in, polished shaft 35 ft 10 in to water level: over 44 ft 2 in, probably c. 50 ft as Xuanzang says; groves round Bakhra = the great forest
quote: I would, therefore, fix its probable original height at about 50 feet;- which would then agree with the measm'ement of Hwen Thsang…The assembly was held, according to Hwen Thsang, at a spot 2-| miles to the south-east of the city, but 1 could find no remains in that direction.
note: 07.03.14 (second council) not found on the ground; Mizutani: disputed.

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: Kesariya stupa (Champaran district)
evidence: upper stupa 68 ft 6 in broad at 62 ft height, on a ruined older stupa, est. 160 ft diam.; mound 62 ft high, 1,400 ft round; local name Deora
quote: That such a practice was not uncommon, w'-e learn from Hwen Thsangj who describes two stupas at VaisMi as having been erected on ancient foundations.
note: See P27 for the identification.

author: Cunningham
name_in_asr: stupa of the Chakravartti Raja Mahadeva
asr_identification: Kesariya stupa, 30 miles NNW of Besarh
evidence: local tradition of Raja Ben Chakravartti; position at the crossing of the Patna-Bettiah and Chapra-Nepal roads; gallery excavated c. 40 years earlier, nothing found
quote: at somewhat less than 200 U (that is, less than 33 miles, or say about 30 miles) to the north-west of VaisMi, which is the exact position of the Kesariya stupa, there was an ancient town which had been deserted for many ages.
note: Agrees with Mizutani and AG 1871.

author: Cunningham

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: Kasia (Gorakhpur district), 35 miles E of Gorakhpur
evidence: ruins: Devisthan/Ramabhar stupa, fort of Matha Kuar, mounds; old channels of the Little Gandak between the ruins
quote: I have little doubt that it should be written ICuda udth the short for the place corresponds, both in position and in name, with the celebrated Kusinagarcc
note: Agrees with Mizutani and AG 1871 (Kasia; Wilson's proposal).

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: Kasia
evidence: Kasia 112 miles NNE of Benares direct (Xuanzang 700 li = 116 mi); 140 miles NW of Vaisali by road (Faxian 23 yojanas); 21+ earthen barrows; local name Matha Kuar
quote: According to Hwen Thsang, Kusinagara was situated at 700 li, or IIG miles to the northeast of Benares. Now Kasla is 112 miles to the north north-east of Benares in direct line.

author: Cunningham
name_in_asr: Kusinagara; sal grove vihar; Asoka stupa; Ajitavati/Hiranyavati
asr_identification: city = mound and village of Anrudhwa; nirvana vihar = mass K at W end of the Matha Kuar mound; Asoka stupa = brick tower A; Hiranyavati = the Hirana stream W of Kasia
evidence: Anrudhwa mound c. 600 ft square (palace), city c. 2,500 ft square, circuit 10,000 ft vs 12 li; vihar 3-4 li NW of city; local name Hirana for the stream
quote: I liave come to the conclusion that the famous city of Kusinagara must have occupied the site of the mound and! village of Anrudhwa…The distance and direction correspond exactly with the site of the great mound now called the Port of Mdthd Kudr.
note: Agrees with Mizutani on the nirvana site. River: Mizutani notes Xuanzang conflated Ajitavati and Hiranyavati.

author: Cunningham
name_in_asr: cremation stupa; large town of the rich Brahman
asr_identification: Ramabhar Tila (= Devisthan), Kasia; Khukhundo (Gorakhpur district) for the Brahman's town
evidence: Ramabhar Tila E of Anrudhwa; old Ghagra crossing below the Rapti, road Kasia-Khukhundo-Kahaon-Bhagalpur; Khukhundo 27 miles from Kasia, ruins covering nearly a square mile, square temple mounds, one excavated
quote: I am, therefore, strongly inclined to identify the JRdmdhlidr TUa with the famous cremation stupa…Of these three, Khuldiundo corresponds best with the description of a large town
note: 06.04.14: AG 1871 revises to Kahaon (preferred to Khukhundo); Mizutani: unknown. Cremation stupa agrees with AG (Devisthan); Mizutani: a mound about ten miles (約十マイル) (disputed).

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: Banaras, between the Barna and the Asi; Sarnath
evidence: statues of Buddha 'turning the wheel' found at Sarnath in 1835-36 (Cunningham) and 1851-52 (Kittoe)
quote: The city of Ban^ras is situated on the left bank of the Ganges, between the ISarnCi Nadi on the north-east, and the uftsi Nala on the south-west.
note: Agrees with Mizutani and AG 1871.

author: Cunningham
name_in_asr: stupa 300 ft high, 2-3 li SW of the Deer Park monastery
asr_identification: Chaukhandi mound, Sarnath (Benares district); Deer Park monastery = mound of Barahipur village
evidence: shaft sunk in the centre of Chaukhandi and widened to 20 ft at 27 ft depth: no relic chamber (fits Xuanzang's commemorative stupa); distance from Barahipur mound half a mile SSW
quote: which, I believe, may be identified with the Chciidcandi mound. At 2 or 3 U (or rather less than lialf a mile) to the south-west of the Beer Park Monastery, II wen Tbsang x^aces a which was no less than 300 feet in height.
note: Agrees with Mizutani (Chaukhandi).

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: Chaukhandi, Sarnath
evidence: centre solid brick; Kittoe exposed three huge buttress-like walls on the E side and two on the W, taken to support the lost upper part
quote: Hwen Thsang’s account is somewhat vague, but I believe his intention was to describe a dome or cupola narrowed at the base, like the neclc of a religious vase reversed.
note: Agrees with Mizutani.

author: Cunningham
note: Sarnath excavated temple: wall decoration compared with Xuanzang's great vihar; no location argued.

author: Cunningham
name_in_asr: stone on which Buddha dried his kashaya
asr_identification: large hollowed squared stone block (now lost) found at Sarnath
evidence: squared block 6 x 3 x 3 ft hollowed underneath into a chamber 4 x 2 ft; since disappeared
quote: I think it highly probable tliai- it the cclehra ted stone
note: Tentative; the robe-drying stone belongs to the three-pond section (07.01.06); Mizutani gives the ponds only.

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: Vairat N of Jaypur (St. Martin), not yet visited
quote: the first place that he visited was Po-li-ye-to-lo, or ’Pariyaira^ which has hcen idcatified by IM. St. Martia with Vairdt, to the northward of Jaypar. This place I have not yet visited
note: Opening of the 1862-63 report; lists the cities 'discovered' with Xuanzang's aid (Ahichhatra, Kosambi, Saketa, Sravasti; Srughna, Madipur, Govisana, Pilosana, Kusapura, Dhopapapura), treated in later passages. Agrees with Mizutani (Bairat).

author: Cunningham
note: Delhi: silence of the pilgrims about Dilli; not a Xiyu ji place.

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: ancient capital on the W bank of the Jumna near Paota/Topra, 66 miles from Thanesar; Topar 'Suh' = Sughan
evidence: Firuz Shah's pillar came from Topar(-Suh), within Srughna; pillar measured 42 ft 7 in, 4 ft 1 in sunk
quote: Now, in this immediate neighbourhood on the western bank of the Jumna, and at a distance of 66 miles from Thanesar, Hwen Thsang x^laces the ancient Capital of Srughna
note: Capital not yet fixed: AG 1871 and Mizutani place it at Sugh (38-40 miles from Thanesar); the name Suh is the only link here.

author: Cunningham
note: Delhi Iron Pillar compared with metal statues described by Xuanzang; not location.

author: Cunningham
note: Mathura: Xuanzang's figures for temples and monasteries; no location.

author: Cunningham
name_in_asr: monastery of Upagupta on a mound, 5-6 li E of the city; stone chamber; dry tank
asr_identification: (identification follows in P45)
quote: place described by Hwen Thsang is a monastery situated on a mound, at G or G li^ or about one mile, to the
note: Summary of Xuanzang's Mathura sites; identification in P45.

author: Cunningham
name_in_asr: monastery of Upagupta; tank where Buddha took exercise and the monkey offered honey
asr_identification: Katra mound, 1 mile W of the old fort of Mathura; tank mound 3 miles SE of the Katra
evidence: recent discovery of important Buddhist remains and old inscriptions in a mound beside a tank 3 miles SE of the Katra; distance 3.5-4 miles by the old road; Anand Tila and Vinayak Tila mound names
quote: This tank mound I take to be the place where Buddha was said to have taken exercise, and where the monkey made his offering of honey…amply sufficient to fix the site of the Uxpaguj}ta monastery at the present Kaira.
note: Differs from Mizutani, who holds 04.07.03 cannot now be located; the Katra view is listed in mz_other_views. Note: Xuanzang puts the monastery E of the city; Katra is W.

author: Cunningham
note: Mathura: decline of Buddhism after Xuanzang's visit (Mahmud's invasion).

note: Duplicate OCR of the previous passage (Mathura, Mahmud's invasion).

author: Cunningham
name_in_asr: dry tank in which the monkey was killed
asr_identification: tank immediately W of the Jail mound (Kunda-Suka monastery), Mathura
evidence: monastery name Kunda-Suka ('dry tank') in inscriptions; pillars, railings, colossal hand 1 ft across (statue 20-24 ft)
quote: as the position of the tank agrees with that assigned by Hwen Thsang to the ‘ dry tank’ in which the monkey was killed, I think there can bo no doubt of the accmacy of my identification.
note: No separate id for the monkey tank; Mizutani: Mathura sites not locatable.

author: Cunningham
note: Mathura statues of the Teacher illustrated by Xuanzang's remark; no location.

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: Khalsi rock within the territory of Srughna; Suh may preserve Sughan
evidence: Khalsi rock: quartz boulder 10 x 10 x 8 ft with edicts of Asoka
quote: I am satisfied with having shown that the inscribed rock of Khalsi is situated within the territory of Srughna
note: Capital not fixed; AG 1871: Sugh.

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: Madawar (Mandawar) near Bijnor, W Rohilkhand; Mayurapura = Mayapur near Hardwar
evidence: distance Paota-Madawar 110 miles by road; old mound half a mile square, 10 ft high, large bricks; fort 300 ft square; deserted in 1114 per the Kanungo
quote: Madipur has been identihed by M. St. Martin ■with Manddwar, a large old town in W estern Eohilhhund near Bijnor. I had made the same identification my-* self before reading M. St. Martin’s remarks
note: Differs from Mizutani, who places Matipura on the E bank of the Ganges opposite Srughna; agrees with AG 1871.

author: Cunningham
name_in_asr: monasteries of Gunaprabha and Sanghabhadra; stupa in mango grove
asr_identification: Madawar: Lalpur mound (Gunaprabha monastery); shrine of Hidayat Shah (Sanghabhadra's monastery); fakir's takia in a mango grove (Sanghabhadra stupa)
evidence: town circuit 20 li fits the old town; Lalpur on a mound 3/4 mile SSE of the Jama Masjid, built of old bricks; Hidayat Shah shrine half a mile N, of old bricks; takia 200 paces WNW in a mango grove
quote: The village of Lfilpur, which is situated on a mound about three-quarters of a mile to the south-south-east of the Jama Masjid, and, which is built partly of old bricks, represents the site of the small monastery of Gunaprabha.
note: Sub-sites of Matipura (no separate ids).

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: edge of the Birwala Tal by the mango grove, Madawar
evidence: mango grove extends 120 paces W to the Birwala Tal
quote: I conclude, therefore, that the Stupa of Yimata Mitra must have stood close to the edge of this tank and on the border of the mangoe grove

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: old fort of Ujain, 1 mile E of Kashipur (Kumaon Terai)
evidence: route 44 kos = 66 miles from Madawar; fort 3,000 x 1,600 ft, circuit 9,000 ft, c. 11,000 ft with the southern suburb mound (Xuanzang 12,000 ft); Dron Sagar tank; bricks 15 x 10 x 2.5 in; walls 30 ft high
quote: I feel quite satisfied that the old fort of JJjoAn represents the ancient city of Govisema which was visited by Hwen Thsang.
note: Agrees with Mizutani and AG 1871.

author: Cunningham
name_in_asr: Govisana temples and Asoka stupa; A-hi-chi-ta-lo, Ahichhatra
asr_identification: Govisana: 14 temple mounds; Asoka's 200-ft stupa not identified; Ahichhatra = Ahichhatr (Adikot)
evidence: solid brick mound 20 ft high near Jagesar Mahadeva, est. 80 ft diameter, too small for a 200-ft stupa
quote: I feel quite unable to offer any identiffcation whatever of the Buddhist remains of Govisana as described by the Chinese pilgrim…This once famous place still preserves its ancient name as Ahiolbhatr
note: Agrees with Mizutani on Ahichhatra (Ramnagar).

author: Cunningham
name_in_asr: Ahi-chhatra; stupa by the serpent tank where Buddha converted the Naga King
asr_identification: ruined fortress of Ahichhatr (Adikot), Ramnagar, Bareli district; Chhatr stupa
evidence: fort an irregular right-angled triangle, sides c. 5,900, 6,100, 7,400 ft, circuit over 3.5 miles (Xuanzang 17-18 li); 32 towers 28-35 ft high; ravines on N and E (Xuanzang's 'natural obstacles'); only existing stupa called Chhatr, read as Ahi-chhatra 'serpent canopy'
quote: Both the size and the peculiar position of the ruined fortress of Alii-chliaira agred
note: Agrees with Mizutani (Ramnagar) and AG 1871. 'Discovered' here (1862-63).

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: temple mounds inside and W of the Ahichhatr fort
evidence: ruins of 20 temples excavated (vs Xuanzang's nine), moulded bricks; temple No. I mound 65 ft 9 in high with a colossal lingam
quote: According to Hwen Thsang there were only nine Brahmanical temples at Alii-clihatra in A. B. 631, all of which would appear to have been dedicated to Siva.
note: Fieldwork on Xuanzang's description of the town.

author: Cunningham
name_in_asr: great stupa where Buddha converted the Serpent King; four small stupas; Naga-hrada
asr_identification: Chhatr mound with eight surrounding mounds, Ahichhatr
evidence: solid brick 40 ft high, 30 ft diam. at top; original hemisphere 50 ft on 15-ft plinth, later casing 12.5 ft (diam. 75 ft); four of the eight surrounding mounds are stupas; no trace of the serpent tank (low ground to the SW)
quote: X have uo doubt, therefore, as to the identity of the Chliair mound .with the Stupa of Hwen Thsang, although I was imablo to discover any certain trace of the tank
note: No separate id for the stupa in the master table.

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: not Soron (Sukara-kshetra); crossing of the Ganges near Sahawar
evidence: route S from Ahichhatra 23-25 miles to the Ganges, crossing near Sahawar (42 miles direct); Soron fort mound a quarter mile long
quote: visited So7^07i, wliioli is undoulDtedly a place of very great antiquity, but which cannot, I think, be the place visited by the Chinese pilgrim
note: First thought Soron, rejected in favour of Atranji-Khera (P60).

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: Atranji-Khera mound, 4 miles S of Karsana (Etah district); Sankisa village (Farrukhabad district)
evidence: not visited; servant's report: mound 3,250 x 2,650 ft at base (circuit c. 2 miles), highest point 44 ft 9 in (Asoka stupa?), two small mounds E, one 165 x 105 ft S; Brahmanical fragments; distance 43 miles direct from Sankisa; proposes 300 li for 200 for both Atranji-Sankisa and Sankisa-Kanoj; Sankisa found by Cunningham in 1842; no trace of the name Kapitha
quote: we can scarcely arrive at auy other conclusion than that the great ruined mound of Atranji is the site of the ancient Piloshanna.
note: 04.14 differs from Mizutani (Bilsar, Etah district); AG 1871 keeps Atranji-Khera (tentative). Sankisa agrees with Mizutani and AG.

author: Cunningham
name_in_asr: Sankisa; three staircases; lion pillar; tank of the Naga
asr_identification: Sankisa: Naga tank = Kandaiya Tal SE of the ruins
evidence: Naga Karewar still offered milk in Vaisakh and when rain is wanted (as in Faxian); Kilah mound 41 ft high, 1,600 x 1,000 ft
quote: The only spot that can he identified with any certainty is the tank of the which still exists to the south-east of the ruins, in the very position ■ described hy Hwen Thsang
note: Agrees with Mizutani on Sankisa.

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: Sankisa; elephant capital possibly = Xuanzang's lion pillar
evidence: ramparts circuit 18,900 ft (Xuanzang 20 li); punch-marked and cast coins; elephant capital neck 2 ft 9.5 in, est. shaft 44 ft 3 in, total c. 52 ft; trunk lost
quote: his circuit of 20 li, or 3^^ miles, being only a little less than my measurement of 18,y00 feet, or 3^ miles. There can he no doubt, therefore, that the place is actually the same
note: Mizutani: the elephant capital is why V. A. Smith rejected Sankisa (04.15.02 disputed); Cunningham argues here that the pilgrims mistook the elephant for a lion.

author: Cunningham
name_in_asr: great monastery with the three staircases
asr_identification: temple of Bisari Devi, Sankisa (alternatively the village mound); three mounds E of the Nivi-ka-kot = three stupas
evidence: excavations at the mounds without result; no base of the pillar found; some villagers place the capital's original site W of the village mound (octagonal hole in a small mound)
quote: I infer, therefore, that the temple of Sisdri Dem most probably occupies the site of the three staircases
note: AG 1871 places the staircases in the central mound (citadel); Mizutani: Sankisa (disputed).

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: Sankisa: village mound as alternative site of the monastery; Paor-Kheria 'Staircase Village' outside the SE gate; Kanoj
evidence: tradition that Sankisa was given to Brahmans c. A.D. 660; Paor-Kheria wholly Brahman; Kanoj 20 x 5 li, Ganges on its E face (also Faxian)
quote: the mound on which the village now stands womd almost certainly be the site of the great monastorf w itli its three holy staircases…Hwen Thsang, who describes Kanoj as being 20 U, or 3-|- miles, in length, and or' 5 li, or three-quarter of a mile, in breadth.
note: Rest of the passage is Harsha's chronology. AG 1871 also cites Paor-Kheria.

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: Kanauj (Farrukhabad district); old bed of the Ganges = Chhoti Ganga / Kali Nadi
evidence: no single site identifiable; ancient city traditionally 3 miles N-S (Haji Harmayan to Miran-ka-Sarai); Kali Nadi flows in the old Ganges channel
quote: I am obliged •:o confess with regret that I have not'becn able to identify
note: Agrees with Mizutani (Kali = Xuanzang's 'Ganges') and AG 1871.

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: Kanauj; Chota Ganga (now carrying the Kali Nadi) = old main channel of the Ganges
evidence: open channel between Sangrampur and the Kali Nadi; citadel triangular, faces c. 4,000 ft
quote: The accounts of Ta Hian and Hwen Thsang, who place Kanoj on the Ganges, are therefore confirmed, not only by the traditions of the people, hut jflso by the fact that the old channel still exists under the name of the Chota Gangd
note: Agrees with Mizutani's reading of the 'Ganges' at Kanauj (= the Kali).

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: ancient Kanauj from Haji Harmayan and the Kshem Kali bastion SW to Makarandnagar on the Grand Trunk Road (3 x c. 1 mile)
evidence: tradition of 84 wards (25 surviving, c. 3/4 sq. mile, implying 2.5 sq. miles); coin find-spots (Bala Pir, Rang Mahal, Makhdum Jahaniya, Makarandnagar, Rajgir mound 3 miles SE)
quote: Kow, this is the very size that is assigned to the old city by Hwen Thsang, who makes its length 20 It, or 3-y- miles, and its breadth 4 or 6 li

author: Cunningham
name_in_asr: great Asoka stupa 6-7 li SE; Asoka stupa NW of the town; three monasteries S
asr_identification: not found SE of Kanauj; NW stupa perhaps at Kapatiya (Kapteswari) village
evidence: searched for the SE stupa on the S bank of the Chota Ganga without result; brick remains near Kapatiya but no large stupa
quote: I conclude, therefore, that Hwen Thsang’s account is most likely right, but I failed in my search for any remains of this vast monument in the position indicated
note: Sub-sites of Kanauj not in the master table; Faxian put the stupa W of the town on the N bank.

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: Navadevakula near Nobatganj opposite Nanamow Ghat, swept away by the Ganges; Ayutho = Kakupur, 1 mile N of Seorajpur (Cawnpore district), alternatively Khara; Ayomukha = Daundiakhera
evidence: change of the Ganges course below the Isan junction leaving an island 6 x 4.5 miles; Xuanzang's total Kanoj-Prayag 1,700 li is c. 100 miles too long, so 600 li read as 60 li (or 700 as 70); footnote alternative Deokali on the Chota Ganga 2 miles below Kanauj
quote: I think it probable that the two places are the same, and that the site was somewhere near Nobatganj…I confess, however, that I am more inclined to adopt the former correction, which places the chief city of Ayutho at Kakupur, and the town of Kayamuhha at Daundiakhera
note: 05.02 differs from Mizutani (Fuhrer's Aphui, Fatehpur district) and rejects Ayodhya on the Ghaghra (Julien, St. Martin); AG 1871 repeats Kakupur. 05.03 differs from Mizutani (Rae Bareli-Pratapgarh area). 05.01.09 as in AG.

author: Cunningham
name_in_asr: Ayutho (= Bagud of the Tibetan books?); O-ye-mu-khi, Ayomukha; Prayaga; tree of the man-eating demon; great sandy plain
asr_identification: Kakupur (not visited); Daundiakhera (Unao district); Allahabad: the Akshay Bat in the fort = the tree and temple
evidence: Kakupur: foundations of large bricks, 'palace' walls (by report); Daundiakhera citadel 385 ft square but town never 20 li round, no Buddhist remains; Akshay Bat underground in a pillared court E of the Ellenborough Barracks, due N of the Asoka pillar; distance Daundiakhera-Prayag 104 miles S road, 115-120 N road; sandy plain since eroded
quote: if I am right in my identification of Ayutlio with Kdhupur, it is almost certain that Ayomuhha must be the same as Haundiakhera…I think there can be little doubt that the famolis tree here described by the Chinese pilgrim is the well known AJcshay Bat
note: 05.02/05.03 differ from Mizutani (see P69). Prayaga and the banyan agree with Mizutani and AG 1871. Daundiakhera admitted doubtful ('must still remain doubtful').

author: Cunningham
note: Allahabad fort legend; legendary history of Kosambi.

author: Cunningham
note: Kosambi in literature (Ratnavali, Udayana); Xuanzang's sandalwood statue mentioned without location.

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: Kosam (Kosambi-nagar) on the Jumna, c. 30 miles above Allahabad
evidence: SW bearing from Prayaga points to the Jumna; Kosam still known as Kosambi-nagar and a Jain resort (Bayley, Siva Prasad); legend of Bakkula places Kosambi on the Jumna
quote: although . the south-west bearing from Praydga or Allahabad, as recorded by Hwen Thsang, points unmistakably to the line of the Jumna…This information was quite sulficient to satisfy me that Kosam was the actual site of the once famous Kosdmhi.
note: Agrees with Mizutani and AG 1871. Suggestion credited to E. C. Bayley (1861).

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: Kosam
evidence: Kosam 31 miles from Allahabad fort (road 35-37 miles); Xuanzang's 50/500 li read as 150 li (15 kos); Akbar-period inscription on the stone pillar names Kausambi-puri; fortress circuit 23,100 ft (4 mi 3 fur), ramparts 30-35 ft, bastions 50-60 ft
quote: it is quite certain that the present Kosam stands on the actual site ,of the ancient Kosdmhi

author: Cunningham
name_in_asr: Kosambi (30 li circuit); two stupas and a cave SW
asr_identification: Kosam; SW angle and the SW sites carried away by the Jumna
evidence: restoring the lost SW angle gives a circuit of 5 mi 7 fur (Xuanzang 30 li = 5 miles); six gates recognized
quote: In three main points therefore of name, size, and position, the present Kosam corresponds most exactly with the ancient Kos4mbi

author: Cunningham
name_in_asr: palace of Udayana with the sandalwood statue under a stone dome
asr_identification: central mound of Kosam with the Jain temple called Deora
evidence: mound locally called Deora 'the Temple'; foundations E and W; Buddhist railing pillars and inscribed pedestal (8th-9th c.) at Bara Garhawa 1,500 ft SW; stupa-sculptured pillar at Chota Garhawa
quote: This description shows that the place must have occupied the position of the great central mass of ruin, which is now covered by a small Jain temple.
note: No separate id for the palace site in the master table.

author: Cunningham
name_in_asr: palace of Udayana with great vihara
asr_identification: Kosam stone pillar and surroundings
evidence: 6th-7th c. inscription 3-4 ft below ground shows the pillar was upright then; Akbar-era inscription naming Kosambipura
quote: This inference is fully hoJ-’ne out by Hwen Thsang’s account of the ancient palace o,f Uddyana

author: Cunningham
name_in_asr: Asoka stupa and dragon cave 8-9 li SW; Asoka stupa and Ghoshila's garden SE (Kui-shi-lo)
asr_identification: SW sites carried away by the Jumna (Prabhasa hill has no cave); Ghoshila garden = Gopsahsa village near Chota Garhawa, SE of Kosam
evidence: river reach to Prabhasa hill bears 12 deg N of W; Prabhasa hill: modern Jain temple, no cavern; four-headed lingam in the fort (Xuanzang's 50 temples)
quote: If Hwen Thsang’s south-west bearing is correct, the holy cave must have been carried away long ago by the encroachment of the Jumna…I believe to be still preserved in Gopsalisa, tbe name of a small village close to Chota Garliaiod.
note: 05.05.03: Mizutani follows Sharma's excavated monastery N of the E gate; Cunningham's Gopsahsa is a village-name match SE of the fort.

author: Cunningham
name_in_asr: monastery with Asoka stupa 200 ft and hair-and-nail stupa SE of Kosambi; Kia-she-pu-lo (Kasapura)
asr_identification: Kosam Khiraj (Hisamabad), 1/4 mile SE of the fort; Kasapura = Sultanpur on the Gomati (ancient Kusapura / Kusabhavanapura), with an old tope near Mahmudpur 5 miles NW
evidence: squared stones in house walls; four railing pillars in two sizes matching the largest and smallest Mathura railings; corner pillar; Kosam-Papamau ghat-Sultanpur 109 miles (Xuanzang 700 li); Sultanpur-Ajudhya 30 miles (170-180 li); no tope found at Sultanpur, tope NW near Mahmudpur by report; fort mound 750 ft square, town c. 2 miles round (Xuanzang 10 li)
quote: this village I believe to have been tbe site of tbe monastery with its lofty Stupa of 200 feet, built by Asoha…I conclude, therefore, that Sultanpur, the ancient Kiisapm’a, is the same place as the Kasapura of Hwen Thsang
note: Sultanpur agrees with Mizutani and AG 1871. 05.05.03: see P78 note (Mizutani: excavated monastery N of the E gate).

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: Saketa = Ajudhya (Ayodhya), Fyzabad district
evidence: Faxian's 'south' corrected to 'north' (Ceylonese route Kosambi-Saketa-Sravasti), his 20 yojanas from Sankisa to 30; tooth-brush tree legend common to Faxian's Sha-chi and Xuanzang's Visakha; Buddha's 6 years at Visakha = 6 (Burmese) / 16 years at Saketa; Visakha the lady of Saketa; coins of Dhana Deva and Visakha-Datta found only at Ajudhya
quote: I hope to show’- in the most satisfactory manner that these two places are identical, and that they are also the same as the Sdheta and Ajudhya of the Hindus.
note: Mizutani gives no identification (05.06 disputed; Smith: Nimkhar); AG 1871 keeps Saketa = Ajudhya. Dhopapapura (Hindu tirtha) in the same passage is not a Xiyu ji place.

author: Cunningham
note: Ayodhya rebuilt by Vikramaditya; Xuanzang's Vikramaditya of Sravasti cited for date only.

author: Cunningham
name_in_asr: great monastery; Asoka stupa 200 ft; tooth-brush tree S of the city, left of the road
asr_identification: Ajudhya: Sugriv Parbat (monastery), Mani Parbat (Asoka stupa), mounds S of the city E of the road
evidence: Sugriv Parbat 500 x 300 ft, rectangular, with interior well and cloistered rooms; Mani Parbat 65 ft high; old road from the S end of the city to Bharat-kund and Sultanpur; city 16 li round (half the present size)
quote: This monastery I would identify Avith the Sngrih Parhat…This monument I would identify with the Mani-Parhai^ AAdiich is still G5 feet' in height
note: Sub-sites of 05.06 (no separate ids).

author: Cunningham
name_in_asr: tooth-brush tree; seats and walk of the four past Buddhas; hair-and-nail stupa
asr_identification: Ajudhya: court-yard with the tombs of Seth and Job (S side of Mani Parbat); Kuber Parbat (hair-and-nail stupa); Ganes-kund (a tank)
evidence: Mani Parbat: earthen core with later masonry; brick stamped with an early 'sh'; local name Bareta for the old city
quote: These places I would identify with the court-yard containing the tombs of Seth and Job…The Stupa I would identify Avith the K^iher-Parbat

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: Ajudhya: the Mahwa tree on the Kuber Parbat now bears the name
evidence: coolies volunteered that the Mahwa tree was a Raja's tooth-brush; same tradition at Gonda (Chilbil shrub)
quote: Both Pa Hian and Hwon Thsang agree in stating that the Bantadhdioan of Saketa was only seven feet high
note: Rest of the passage (Hatila / Asokpur) not linked to Xuanzang.

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: Sahet-Mahet on the S bank of the Rapti (Gonda/Bahraich)
evidence: Sravasti N of Saketa (Xuanzang, Ceylonese books, Puranas); Faxian 8 yojanas = 56 miles; Xuanzang's 500 li corrected to 350 li = 58 miles, the distance from Ajudhya
quote: I would correct his distance by the nearest round number of 350 li or 58 miles* to bring it into accordance with the other.
note: Agrees with Mizutani and AG 1871.

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: Sahet-Mahet, between Akaona and Balrampur
evidence: colossal statue of Buddha with an inscription naming Sravasti found by Cunningham; crescent-shaped city 1 1/3 mile along the old Rapti bank; ramparts 25-50 ft
quote: in which I discovered a colossal statue of Buddha with an inscription containing the name of Sravasti itself

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: Sahet-Mahet
evidence: circuit of the ramparts 17,300 ft (over 3 1/4 miles) = Xuanzang's 20 li, which he gave for the palace; parapet wall 10 ft thick on the river face
quote: The whole circuit of the old earthen ramparts, according to my sm’vey, is 17,300 feet, or upwards of Similes. Now, this is the exact size of 20 li or 3| miles which Hwen Thsang gives to the xsalace alone

author: Cunningham
note: History of Sravasti (Virudhaka's tank, Vikramaditya); no location.

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: Sahet-Mahet
evidence: name Sahet = Pali Sawet; Set-met; desolation of the site
quote: Similarly the modern name of Sdhet is evidently only a variation of the Pali Sdimi.
note: Name argument for the identification.

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: Sahet-Mahet; Jetavana = the mass of ruins half a mile S of the nearest opening in the S rampart
evidence: local name Savitri (from the keeper of Pir Barana's tomb); Faxian 1,200 paces vs Xuanzang 5-6 li; route through the holy places E of the ruins makes 3/4 mile
quote: But as the only mass of ruins which can possibly be identified with the Jetavmia is exactly half a mile from the nearest opening in the south rampart of the old city
note: Mizutani gives no identification for 06.01.04 (status unknown); AG 1871 not coded for it.

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: Jogini-jharia mound S of Sahet-Mahet
evidence: ruined monastery mound not over 1,000 x 700 ft (one-third of the area in the Ceylonese annals); dimensions not given by the pilgrims
quote: but the ruined mound of the monastery still exists, and its dimensions do not exceed 1,000 feet in length by 700 feet in breadth.
note: Mizutani gives no identification for 06.01.04.

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: the great mound called Jogini-jharia (the monastery proper); ruins E and N = holy places outside it
evidence: Ceylonese description (vihara, cells, ambulatory, tanks, gardens, 18-cubit wall)
quote: it is certain that the original monastery must have been confined to the Jogini’^hao'ia only
note: See P93-P96.

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: great rectangular mound half a mile from the SW corner of Sahet-Mahet
evidence: mound 1,000 ft NE-SW x 700 ft, rim of cells 8-12 ft high; central line falls on the Sobhnath mound inside the city's SW angle; excavations in each eminence after clearing jungle
quote: The great mound of ruins, which I propose to identify with the Jetavana, is situated just. half a mile distant from the south-west corner of the old city.

author: Cunningham
name_in_asr: two stone pillars at the E gate of the Jetavana (dome / elephant; wheel / ox in Faxian)
asr_identification: two slight eminences 300 ft E of the Jetavana mound
evidence: colossal stone Buddha found (inscribed), probably buried before Faxian's visit; no remains of the pillars
quote: There are no remains of these pillars, but there are two slight eminences only 300 feet distant from the monastery which may have been the basements on which the pillars stood
note: Also uses the Sravasti pillar discrepancy to defend the Sankisa elephant capital (cf. P62-P63).

author: Cunningham
name_in_asr: three gulfs (Devadatta, Kokali, Chancha); pair of temples (Buddhist and 'shadow-covered' Brahmanical)
asr_identification: tanks near the Jetavana mound: Bhulanan (Devadatta), Lambhua Tal (Kokali), nameless tank 2,200 ft S (Chancha); ruins S and T E and W of the road from the city
evidence: Bhulanan tank 600 x 250 ft within 200 ft of the SE corner; Kokali tank 200 ft S of it; Chancha tank 600 x 400 ft, 2,200 ft further S (Xuanzang 800 paces)
quote: The exact correspondence of position of these three tanks with the three great fissures or gulfs of the Buddhist legends offers a very strong confirmation of the correctness of identification of the Jogini-laria mound with the great Jetavana monastery.
note: Sub-sites of Sravasti (no separate ids).

author: Cunningham
name_in_asr: stupa where Maudgalyayana tried to loosen Sariputra's girdle; Wood of the Recovered Eyes (Andhavana)
asr_identification: shrine of Pir Barana at Husen Jot, 700 ft NW of the Jetavana; Andhavana = Rajgarh Gulariya village, in a large grove 2/3 mile NW
evidence: Andhavana 4 li NW of the monastery (both pilgrims); old trees about the village; no trace of Asoka's stupa and pillar (bricks taken for the shrine)
quote: This position is now represented exactly by the village of Hdjgarh Qulariya^ which is situated in the midst of a very large grove of trees.
note: 06.01.13: Mizutani gives no identification (unknown); not in AG 1871 as coded.

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: Ora-jhar mound, upwards of a mile SE of the Jetavana
evidence: Faxian's NE bearing corrected to SE; Ora-jhar 4,000 ft SE of the mounds identified with the Brahmanical temple (Xuanzang: over 4 li E of it); solid earth mound 70 ft high
quote: 1 am therefore quite satisfied that it is the remains of the great Vilidvct of the JPicrvvdrdma, or Eastern Monastery.
note: No separate id for the Purvarama in the master table.

author: Cunningham
asr_identification: Ora-jhar mound (footnote defends the SE bearing against Beal)
evidence: Faxian's NE would place it in the Rapti; Ora-jhar lies SE by E of the Jetavana; mound No. 6 an alternative but too low
quote: 1 liave now considered the whole subject over ngiiin, and I adhere to my first identification.

author: Cunningham
name_in_asr: Visakha's stupa; place where Virudhaka halted; stupa of the massacred Sakya maidens; Virudhaka's tank
asr_identification: small mound NE of Ora-jhar (Visakha's stupa); nameless tank S of Visakha's temple (Virudhaka's tank)
evidence: small mound 8 ft high, excavated 11 ft: solid large bricks 12 x 9 x 3 in, 40 ft diameter; traces of steps on the E slope of Ora-jhar; nine ruined monasteries and ten temple foundations near the city
quote: I have little doubt*' that this is the stu]pa which VisdkUd built on the spot where Buddha had overcome the Brahmans in argument.

author: Cunningham
name_in_asr: stupa containing the complete body of Kasyapa (N of the town); Kasyapa's birthplace
asr_identification: Tanda (Tadwa), W of Sahet-Mahet: brick stupa at the SW corner of the mound
evidence: stupa at least 70 ft in diameter; lingam on top prevented excavation; mound c. 1,400 x 1,000 ft (60 bighas); tank N of the mound; temple remains E
quote: The stupa on the mound must certainly represent the latter monument, because the tank precludes the possibility of any other having existed to the northward of it.
note: Mizutani: disputed, no identification (Tadwa is listed among others' views: Cunningham, Beal, Legge).
